nodes.title: CI/CD : Automated Spell Check for Blog Content (Typos Detection)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, there is no automated mechanism to catch spelling mistakes specifically in blog content. As a result, typos often go unnoticed during development and code review, and eventually get merged into production. This affects the professionalism, readability, and quality of the website.

- there many typos which have to fix and fixing all this manually takes too much time

### Proposed Solution

Introduce an automated spell-check step in the CI/CD pipeline that:

- Runs on every pull request that modifies files inside /blog/** (or relevant blog directory).
- Uses a tool like typos (or an equivalent spell-checker).
- Fails the CI check if critical spelling errors are detected.
- Allows a configurable ignore list (.typos.toml) for valid technical terms, names, or abbreviations.
- Provides clear, actionable error messages pointing to the exact file and line with the typo.

### Alternatives Considered

- Relying on manual review only – Rejected because it does not scale, is inconsistent, and still allows many typos to slip through.
- Running spell checks only before releases – Rejected because this delays feedback and makes fixes more costly and cumbersome.
- Using general linting tools instead of a dedicated spell checker – Rejected because most linters do not properly handle natural language in Markdown/blog content.

### Additional Information

- This change aligns with best practices followed by many open-source projects that use automated spell-checking in CI for documentation and blog content.
- The action can be initially configured in a permissive mode (with exclusions) and tightened over time as false positives are handled.

nodes.title: feat: CI/CD: Duplicate Issue Detection and Automatic Marking
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, duplicate issues and pull requests are often created in the repository, leading to redundant discussions, repeated work, and extra maintenance overhead for maintainers. There is no automated mechanism in the CI/CD pipeline to detect potential duplicates and flag them proactively.

### Proposed Solution

I propose adding an automated duplicate issue detection mechanism in the CI/CD workflow that:

- Scans newly created issues and pull requests for similarity with existing ones.
- Identifies potential duplicates based on title, description, and labels.
- Automatically marks suspected duplicates with a label such as possible-duplicate.
- Adds a bot comment suggesting existing related issues with links.
- Optionally closes the issue if an exact match is found (configurable behavior).

### Alternatives Considered

- Manual review by maintainers: Rejected because it does not scale and increases workload.
- GitHub issue templates only: Helpful but does not prevent duplicate submissions.
- Strict issue submission rules: Too restrictive and may discourage contributions.

### Additional Information

- This feature would be especially useful for large repositories with frequent contributions.
- Can be implemented using GitHub Actions with existing tools like issue similarity bots or custom scripts.
- Similar functionality is used in repositories like Kubernetes and TensorFlow.

nodes.title: Clarify platform support table and deprecation notes in README
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

The platform support section in the README mixes current support details with historical deprecation notes (e.g., Windows 7/8 removal in Electron 23) in paragraph form. This can be slightly hard to scan for new users trying to quickly understand which platforms are supported today.

### Proposed Solution

Convert the platform support section into a concise table

Separate current supported platforms from historical deprecation notes

Add a short “Last updated” note to reduce confusion about version-specific support

### Alternatives Considered

Option 1: Minimal

Keep the platform support section as-is and rely on release notes for clarification.

Option 2: Moderate

Add brief inline headings (e.g., “Current Support”, “Deprecated Platforms”) without changing the overall structure.

Option 3: Slightly More Detailed

Move historical deprecation details to a separate section or link to Electron’s versioning documentation instead of including them inline.

If you want it more formal or more GitHub-issue–style, I can tighten it further.

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Add support for nv12 pixel format to offscreen rendered shared texture
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Currently, when creating offscreen rendering BrowserWindow with `useSharedTexture` only 2 pixel formats are supported: 

```ts
sharedTexturePixelFormat?: ('argb' | 'rgbaf16');
```

I want to pass those textures to hardware accelerated video encoder (apple silicon), which expect `nv12` (yuv) pixel format. Otherwise it has to perform a translation, which wastes performance considerably.

### Proposed Solution

It would be optimal if `sharedTexturePixelFormat` would accept more pixel formats, especially some accepted by hardware video encoders

### Alternatives Considered

I consider creating a Metal shader that will translate those textures before passing them to encoder

### Additional Information

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

When using 'retina' display and I need 1000x1000 shared texture from `paint` event, I'd expect I only need to create 500x500 window, as it will paint 1000x1000 physical pixels.

### Actual Behavior

Currently 1000x1000 window on retina (pixel ratio 2) produces 1000x1000 texture, so I imagine it captures 2000x2000 texture and scales it down to 1000x1000, potentially wasting a lot of performance and resources.

nodes.title: Native modules are built without support for macOS < 13.5
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

40.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.2

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

39

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Electron v40 supports macOS 12 and above. Native Node modules should also be built with support for macOS 12 and above.

### Actual Behavior

Native modules are built with support for macOS 13.5 and above.

They do not work on macOS 12–13.5.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Repro:

```bash
npx create-electron-app@latest my-app --template=webpack
cd my-app
npm i fs-xattr
npm start
otool -l node_modules/fs-xattr/build/Release/xattr.node
```

The output includes:

```
    minos 13.5
      sdk 26.2
```

Some libs work around it, e.g., [better-sqlite3](https://github.com/WiseLibs/better-sqlite3/blob/27cb07b5926652ae0e601dc26a35714128692f18/deps/common.gypi#L59).

This happened because Node.js [increased their minimum supported macOS version](https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/8b4022177750530d2c142a5a0349d98fb82f16e2) to 13.5 as part of Node.js 24.0.0.

Now native Node modules compile against that version.

We might want to lower it again in Electron for as long as we support macOS <= 13.4.

More information: https://electronhq.slack.com/archives/CB6CG54DB/p1770224778182279

Discovered by @indutny-signal. 🙏

nodes.title: SecCodeCheckValidity error -67062 on macOS 26 (Tahoe)
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for an issue that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

32.2.7 (via VS Code 1.108.2)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.2 (Tahoe) - Build 25C56

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Expected Behavior

Running an Electron app from the command line should not print code signing errors when the code signature is valid.

### Actual Behavior

When running VS Code (or any Electron app) from the CLI, the following error is printed to stderr:

```
[0204/102237.819836:ERROR:electron/shell/common/mac/codesign_util.cc:109] SecCodeCheckValidity: Error Domain=NSOSStatusErrorDomain Code=-67062 "(null)" (-67062)
```

Error code -67062 = `errSecCSSignatureInvalid`

However, the code signature is actually **valid** according to macOS:

```
$ codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 /Applications/Visual\ Studio\ Code.app
/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app: valid on disk
/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app: satisfies its Designated Requirement

$ spctl --assess --verbose /Applications/Visual Studio Code.app
/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app: accepted
source=Notarized Developer ID
```

This appears to be Electron's internal `SecCodeCheckValidity` call in `codesign_util.cc` failing on macOS 26, even though the signature is valid.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

- This issue has been reported in VS Code: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/204085 (locked, tagged as upstream Electron issue)
- The error is cosmetic and doesn't affect functionality
- Fresh reinstall via Homebrew does not resolve the issue
- Occurs on macOS 26.2 (Tahoe) with Intel Mac (x86_64)


nodes.title: Retry tests in CI automatically when they fail
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

In CI, when tests are flaky and fail, we need to re-run them manually. This is annoying, costs time, and costs computing hours.

### Proposed Solution

Chromium has a nice solution where if a test fails, CI re-runs that single specific test automatically before reporting failure.

If we adopted that for Electron, we'd save maintainers time and we'd reduce our cloud bill. (We'd re-run just the failed test, not the whole test suite.)

### Alternatives Considered

Re-run all tests automatically as a first step. Would already be better than the current solution.

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron should not attempt to access org.bluez service unless Bluetooth APIs are explicitly used.

### Actual Behavior

On running `npx electron`, Electron triggers a D-Bus call to org.bluez, causing errors in system logs when BlueZ is not installed:
```bash
dbus-daemon[754]: [system] Activating via systemd: service name='org.bluez' unit='dbus-org.bluez.service' requested by ':1.1002' (uid=1000 pid=105122 comm="/home/username/electron-bluetooth-test/node_modules/" label="unconfined")
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Output can be seen using `journalctl -f`.
